annotation.method: Codex freshly read the complete 20-page paper in physical-PDF order, surveyed every named proved result and rigorous derivation, compared candidates with the frozen Mathlib and importable NumStability baselines, and privately formalized the selected theorem before packaging it.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P25 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 1.1, the sharpened supported power-series norm bound
rejected_candidates.reason: Its proof is a direct triangle-inequality and termwise maximum comparison using standard Mathlib infinite-series facts. It has no substantial NumStability dependency for T1 or T2 and is materially easier than the selected complete practical bound.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lemma 4.1, the two-generator matrix-power norm inequality
rejected_candidates.reason: The proof is short submultiplicative norm and power algebra. It is not sufficiently difficult for T3 and does not need a substantial importable NumStability result.
The paper proves only a short logarithm and ceiling comparison showing the correction cannot exceed the previous scaling parameter. It is too easy for T3 and has no tier-specific library dependency.
These floating-point bounds are cited from earlier sources rather than proved in this paper, so the required statement-and-proof source text is absent.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Algorithms 3.1, 5.1, and 6.1 and the numerical comparisons in Sections 5-7
rejected_candidates.reason: These are algorithm descriptions, heuristic acceptance tests, and experiments rather than additional universally proved conclusions with source proofs.

T1.decision: Skipped. No source-faithful proved task needs exactly one substantial importable NumStability result that makes L substantially faster than N.

T2.decision: Skipped. No source-backed proved task needs at least two distinct substantial importable NumStability results.

T3.decision: Use both parts of Theorem 4.2 in a faithful Banach-algebra form, retaining the ordinary p,p+1 bound, the even 2p,2p+2 specialization, the cutoff thresholds, and the infinite-series conclusion.

selection_policy: Use only conclusions explicitly stated and proved in the paper.
Express the paper's maximum power-root parameter by an equivalent nonnegative scalar certificate for the indicated generator powers.
Express the radius-of-convergence premise by the absolute scalar majorant summability actually used in the proof.
Retain both the ordinary and even cases of Theorem 4.2 rather than selecting the easy Lemma 4.1 alone.
Do not turn cited bounds, heuristic tests, or numerical experiments into benchmark theorems.
Keep every public definition paper-scoped and free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only after comparison with the complete frozen NumStability source, its importable compiled subset, and Mathlib.
